_: THE CHAPTER REGISTER. read.html walks this and nothing else. A chapter with no `file` shows THE UNWRITTEN PAGE — never a placeholder.
_law: No chapter publishes before the thing it describes.
title: The Book of the Dead
subtitle: How this machine was built, written against the machine
plateNote: This band was read from the live system at the hour of writing. It has not been updated since.

chapters.title: The Beach
chapters.blurb: A man comes out of the sea holding the only object that can release a thousand souls, and what he wants is a cheeseburger.
chapters.why: The frame. The last human scene in the book, and the one chapter with no apparatus — the prologue carries no bands because it makes no claim a probe could check.

chapters.title: The Siege of Amenti
chapters.blurb: A midnight raid on the Fourth of July, the gates breached, and a captain who does not come back with his crew.
chapters.why: The emerald heart comes out of this chapter — the jewel at the fulcrum of the docket scale, and the reason there is a man on a beach at all.

chapters.title: The Specification
chapters.blurb: The halls, the living library and the emerald tablets — in one head before there was anything to build with.
chapters.why: The mythology is not a frame laid over the software. It is the requirements document the software was built to satisfy, and this chapter has to establish that before a single line of code appears.

chapters.title: The Three Refusals
chapters.blurb: Amenti refuses loss. Hades refuses memory, and holds the court. Valhalla refuses return.
chapters.why: Three keys are not three powers. A key that only opens is decoration — what makes them load-bearing is what each one will not do.

chapters.title: The Manifest of the Fleet
chapters.blurb: Every file and its office, and the six that no manifest named.
chapters.why: Half-written already as a pane. The reading is live: the manifest reports what is aboard, and it found files nothing had ever declared.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.blurb: Local, deploy, live. Hundreds of times.
chapters.why: The loop is the work. Most accounts of building software skip it because it is repetitive — which is precisely why it belongs in a book about what building actually costs.

chapters.title: Built at Sea
chapters.blurb: Thousands of probes. A ship that cannot make port, and the difference between construction and navigation.
chapters.why: Book Zero ends where the Flying Dutchman is explained: not a metaphor for hardship, but for a vessel whose repairs all happen underway.

chapters.title: The Roster
chapters.blurb: One thousand and eleven souls in a flat file, and why the list is a boundary rather than a verdict.
chapters.why: Waiting on nothing. The roster is stable and the chapter can be written as soon as Book Zero is out.
